what: Every deck game read ply by ply under each rating arm.
note_live: 'live' is the prototype's own path: the game is rescored from ply 1 to ply t, so ply t sees only plies 1 to t. It is the one curve that reads the same way for all three arms. 'whole_game' is the single bidirectional pass, where every ply sees the finished game.
note_anomaly: Attention, the per-move deviation and the suspicion score are recorded for the served arm only. The trained detector was fitted on that arm's features, so running it on another arm's outputs would produce a number nobody measured.

games.label: Sides separated

headers.Event: Lichess rated blitz game (RatingNet held-out test partition)

games.behavior: A widely mismatched game the gap-weighted arm separates and the main model does not.
games.reason: A showcase, not a typical case: its gap-weighted improvement is at the 99.95th percentile of the 10,544 test games whose players are at least 300 points apart.
games.caveat: Black's clock starts at half the stated time control, so this is a berserked arena game. The clock is an input to the rating model and to every detector, so no single cause should be read into this game's scores.

distribution_context.subgroup: held-out test games whose players are at least 300 points apart
distribution_context.note: Improvement is the mean of a game's two absolute errors under the main model minus the same under the gap-weighted arm, so positive favors the latter. The per-side MAE values are asserted against the separation table's own figures.
distribution_context.produced_by: analysis/scripts/wide_gap_separation_context.py, run on the HPC against attn_tuned__best.csv and mirror_arm_a__best.csv
